clue.text: Spare holy man in church to give absolution

indicators.note: in tells us the pieces before it sit inside the church abbreviation

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
spare in the sense of thin means lean
S is the abbreviation for saint

explanation.surface: A thrifty clergyman visits church to grant forgiveness to sinners.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spare' looks like a verb (spare a sinner), but it is the adjective meaning thin.
explanation.definitionFit: To cleanse someone spiritually is to purify them of sin, which is what absolution does.

clue.text: Pop is to fib about alcoholic drink

indicators.note: about means the word for a fib goes around the drink

parts.note: a fib is a lie
mead is a fermented honey drink

explanation.surface: Someone is going to lie about how much alcohol they have had.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pop' is not the start of a sentence about a father: it is fizzy soft drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Pop is a fizzy soft drink, and a lime-flavoured lemonade is one example.

clue.text: Tailor has fitting interrupted by attorney

indicators.note: interrupted by means the word for fitting is broken open by the attorney

parts.note: fitting means apt, suitable
DA is a district attorney in the US

explanation.surface: A tailor's fitting session is cut short when a lawyer barges in.
explanation.definitionFit: To tailor something is to modify it to suit, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Badly prepared ham cost appetite

indicators.note: badly prepared suggests food made wrongly, so the letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: A poorly cooked and expensive ham puts you off your food.
explanation.definitionFit: Having the stomach for something means having the appetite for it.

clue.text: Record-breaker gives up husband for poet

indicators.note: gives up means the record-breaker surrenders one of its letters

parts.note: a record-breaker is a champion

explanation.surface: A sporting star abandons her husband for a man of verse.
explanation.walkthrough: Thomas Campion was an English poet and composer of the early 1600s.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas Campion is an Elizabethan poet and songwriter, the definition naming his calling.

clue.text: Bill can get girl for performance

parts.note: AC, short for account, is a bill
a tin is a can
G is an abbreviation for girl

explanation.surface: A man called Bill manages to win a girlfriend for the show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bill' looks like a man's name and 'can' a verb; they are an account and a tin.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting is the art of performing on stage, so a performance is a synonym.

clue.text: Dolly eats chicken in ancient temple

indicators.note: eats means the singer's surname takes the bird inside it

parts.note: Dolly Parton is the country singer
a hen is a chicken

explanation.surface: A celebrity singer has a chicken dinner at an ancient shrine.
explanation.definitionFit: The Parthenon is the famous temple to Athena on the Acropolis in Athens.

clue.text: Not allowed to reach conclusion

parts.note: something not allowed is out, ruled out
to come to a place is to reach it

explanation.surface: A ruling says a decision must not be arrived at.
explanation.definitionFit: An outcome is the result or end of a process, a synonym of conclusion.

clue.text: Inept lads lack involvement in hanky-panky

indicators.note: involvement suggests things tangled together, so the letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: Clumsy young men who stay uninvolved miss out on the fun.
explanation.walkthrough: SLAP AND TICKLE is old British slang for playful kissing and fondling.
explanation.definitionFit: Both phrases are playful slang for amorous fooling about, so they are synonyms.

clue.text: Girl takes part in requiem mass

indicators.note: takes part in says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A young woman sings in a funeral service.
explanation.definitionFit: Emma is a female first name, and crosswords use girl for any such name.

clue.text: Alumnus's able to read, write and rub out

parts.note: OB, old boy, is a former pupil
someone able to read and write is literate

explanation.surface: A former student shows off his literacy and his eraser.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'and' joins the pieces to the definition; 'read, write' together describe one word.
explanation.definitionFit: To obliterate is to wipe out entirely, a stronger synonym of erase.

clue.text: Ray set about reading words of comfort repeatedly

indicators.note: set about means the fish is placed around the letter for reading

parts.note: a manta is a large ray
R stands for reading, one of the three Rs

explanation.surface: A man named Ray settles down to read soothing phrases over and over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ray' looks like a man's name; it is the fish.
explanation.definitionFit: A mantra is a phrase chanted again and again to calm or focus the mind.

clue.text: Criticise article about ancient temple

parts.note: to pan is to criticise harshly
the is the definite article
on means about, concerning

explanation.surface: Someone attacks a magazine piece about a temple of antiquity.
explanation.definitionFit: The Pantheon in Rome is a temple to all the gods built in antiquity.

clue.text: Close call for new starter making electrical connection

indicators.note: starter places the letter for new at the very front

parts.note: earthing is connecting a circuit to the ground

explanation.surface: An electrician's apprentice nearly got a shock wiring up a socket.
explanation.definitionFit: A near thing is an idiom for a narrow escape, just like a close call.

clue.text: One replying to resolution on study

indicators.note: in a down clue, on puts the resolution above the study

parts.note: to ponder is to study, think over

explanation.surface: Someone answers a committee's resolution after thinking about it.
explanation.definitionFit: A responder is a person who answers, a direct noun synonym.

clue.text: Mountains with points

parts.note: and means together with
E and S are compass points

explanation.surface: A range of peaks bristling with sharp tips.
explanation.definitionFit: The Andes are the long mountain range running down South America.

clue.text: Luxembourg possesses a capital

parts.note: L is the international vehicle code for Luxembourg
possesses means has

explanation.surface: Luxembourg is a country with its own capital city.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface invites Luxembourg City; the capital meant is in Tibet.
explanation.definitionFit: Lhasa is the chief city of Tibet, its seat of government.

clue.text: Careworn author

definitions.meaning: H Rider ... wrote King Solomon's Mines

explanation.definitionFit: Haggard means drawn and tired; it is also the surname of the Victorian novelist Rider Haggard.

clue.text: Old actor keeps transport in Norway

indicators.note: keeps means the actor holds the vehicle inside

parts.note: an old stager is a veteran performer
a van is a means of transport

explanation.surface: A veteran performer keeps his own vehicle while living in Norway.
explanation.walkthrough: Stavanger is a port city in south-west Norway; the definition names where it is.
explanation.definitionFit: Stavanger is a city on the Norwegian coast, so it lies within that country.

clue.text: Knight wears colour that's intense

indicators.note: wears means the knight is put inside the colour like clothing

parts.note: violet is a colour
N is knight in chess notation

explanation.surface: A knight dressed in a vivid shade looks striking.
explanation.definitionFit: Violent can mean extremely strong or intense, as in a violent storm or violent colour.

clue.text: English couple admitting an issue

indicators.note: admitting means the word for couple lets in the other word

parts.note: to mate is to pair up or couple

explanation.surface: An English pair adopts a child as their offspring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'issue' looks like a noun (children) but is the verb, to come out.
explanation.definitionFit: To emanate is to flow or come out from a source, as to issue does.

clue.text: Keeps including tenor in the musical score

indicators.note: including means the word for keeps holds the tenor's letter

parts.note: to save something is to keep it

explanation.surface: A tenor's part is preserved in the written music.
explanation.definitionFit: Staves are the sets of five lines on which a musical score is written.

clue.text: Sceptic acting so badly

indicators.note: badly means the letters perform poorly, out of order

explanation.surface: A doubter thinks the performance was poor.
explanation.definitionFit: An agnostic doubts whether God's existence can be known, so is a religious sceptic.

clue.text: Trouble in gold market

parts.note: or is gold in heraldry
to deal in goods is to market them

explanation.surface: There is trouble on the gold exchange.
explanation.definitionFit: An ordeal is a painful experience, a period of trouble.

clue.text: Dickens settled up

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: settled somewhere means lived there

explanation.surface: Charles Dickens paid his bills in full.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dickens' looks like the novelist but is the mild oath, as in 'what the dickens?'.
explanation.definitionFit: In exclamations like what the dickens, the word stands for the devil.

clue.text: Doctor valued live entertainment

indicators.note: to doctor something is to tamper with it, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A doctor appreciates live shows.
explanation.definitionFit: Vaudeville is a variety stage entertainment of songs, comedy and acts.

clue.text: Medicine bottle essential when losing heart

indicators.note: losing heart means the word drops its central letter

parts.note: vital means essential

explanation.surface: A medicine bottle is crucial when someone is feeling low.
explanation.definitionFit: A vial is a small glass container for liquid medicine.

clue.text: Bill and Don's home?

parts.note: a bill is a poster, an ad
to don clothes is to dress

explanation.surface: Asking where two men named Bill and Don live.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bill' and 'Don' look like names; they are a poster and a verb meaning to put on.
explanation.definitionFit: An address identifies where someone lives, so it stands for home; the question mark flags the loose fit.

clue.text: Is speaker a follower?

parts.note: is contracts to 's, giving S
a talker is someone who speaks

explanation.surface: Asking whether a public speaker is also a disciple.
explanation.definitionFit: A stalker is someone who obsessively follows another person.
